previous_description: Represents a named resource subject to security controls, defining the operations that can be performed on it and optional field-level access restrictions. Acts as the resource component in subject-action-resource access control triples per NIST SP 800-53 AC-3.
definition: A protected object in an access control model — an API, database, file, service, UI area or stream — named as the target of authorization decisions and owning the set of ResourceOperations permitted on it and any FieldAccessControls over its fields. It is the 'object' of a subject-action-object triple, not the grant, rule or operation applied to it.

distinguish_from.when: the thing protected is a logical information asset (e.g. customer PII) governed by InformationRight grants and classification, independent of the system resource that stores or exposes it
the element is a specific verb (read, approve, export) permitted on the resource rather than the resource itself
the element is a grant of an action on a resource assigned to a role, rather than the resource being protected
the restriction applies to a single field's masking or redaction inside a resource rather than to the resource as a whole

standard_reference: NIST SP 800-53 AC-3 (Access Enforcement) — protected object; XACML 3.0 Resource attribute category
code_evidence: A route group, controller or API path prefix wrapped by an authorization guard or middleware (e.g. @PreAuthorize, router.use(requireAuth), [Authorize]) that names the protected resource

A resource identifier string used as the object argument in permission checks (e.g. can(user, 'update', 'invoice'), enforcer.enforce(sub, 'orders', act)) or as a resource entry in a Casbin/OPA/IAM policy file
A database table, bucket or topic declared in an IAM/RLS/ACL configuration (e.g. Postgres row-level security policy, S3 bucket policy, Kafka ACL) restricting which principals may operate on it

attribute_descriptions.name: resource
attribute_descriptions.description: Canonical identifier of the protected object as used in authorization checks — e.g. an API path pattern ('/api/orders/*'), table name, bucket URI or permission-string resource key; set it to the exact value enforcement code matches against.

attribute_descriptions.name: description
attribute_descriptions.description: Free-text explanation of what the resource contains or exposes and why it requires protection; set it when the identifier alone does not convey sensitivity or scope.

notes: Overlaps with InformationEntity; the spec should state that SecureResource is the system-level container and InformationEntity the logical asset. Permission.resource and AccessCondition reference resources by string rather than by relationship—consider aligning. The type enum lacks 'queue'/'topic' (folded into stream?) and 'object-storage'; no classification attribute exists despite DataClassification governing it.
